💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ruben Amorim insisted that he and his AC Milan team are not getting carried away despite hammering Frosinone, and are simply focusing on the next game.
  • Industry observers note that milan were in a rampant mood tonight at San Siro, as they put five goals past Massimiliano Alvini’s side and it could have been more in truth.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ruben Amorim insisted that he and his AC Milan team are not getting carried away despite hammering Frosinone, and are simply focusing on the next game.

Industry observers note that milan were in a rampant mood tonight at San Siro, as they put five goals past Massimiliano Alvini’s side and it could have been more in truth. Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all scored, in addition to an own-goal that opened the scoring.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was key that the Rossoneri build on their victory over Genoa before the break, especially given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus all won earlier in the round. In addition to that, several individuals shone and the team showed the levels that they are capable of.

Recent findings suggest that now, the challenge is to follow it up and get back on course in the Europa League in Greece on Thursday night. Amorim spoke to Sky after the final whistle to reflect on what was a very positive night for his side, with his words relayed by MilanNews.

Is that the best Milan performance since you have been here?

It has been revealed that “It’s a good feeling, but it’s not just the result: it’s also about consistency throughout the 90 minutes of the match, but now we’re thinking about the next one. It’s always like that at this club, always thinking about the next one.

Recent findings suggest that “Tonight we played well, we were intelligent, courageous, and it showed towards the end of the match. We were tired, yet Frosinone continued to make transitions, but we managed to control them well.

Sources indicate that “We could have even scored more goals. Perhaps in the middle of the first half we struggled a little and we need to improve in one-on-one situations defensively, but anyway, it was a good night for us tonight.”.

Are you happy for Gonçalo Ramos? How is he?

“We can’t lose any more players. All our players can play every game, but we have little time to recover for the Europa League, so we can’t risk anything. It was better to take him off.

In a recent development, “I imagine he wasn’t happy, but I’m still happy for him, for his goal, especially for the 2-0. It was a goal that made the difference in a match against a team that is very strong in one-on-one transitions.”.

Is Rabiot one of the best you’ve ever coached?

According to recent reports, “I don’t want to say he could have had a better career because he played at PSG. Now he’s here at Milan and we want him to stay.

“Obviously, he’s a player who can play as a number 10, as an attacking midfielder, he can also play as a number 8, he can also play as a slightly deeper playmaker, even if he doesn’t like it.

“He’s definitely one of the best players I’ve ever coached, he’s one of the best midfielders in Europe right now.”.

What will you say ahead of Olympiacos?

“The first thing I’ll say is that we have to win the match: if we don’t, then it will be really difficult to qualify for the next stage. Then I think that with Rabiot and Pulisic’s characteristics of playing between the lines, when they can’t play, we have to play and approach the game differently.

“But that’s not an excuse. I said the same things against Ferencváros: we should have played a different game and gotten a different result, but what I’m trying to say is that if we don’t win the match, it will be really difficult and things will go badly for us.

It has been revealed that “Then, if we exit the Europa League, we’ll only play once a week and many players won’t play enough. However, I think that if we stay in Europe, we can play more and everyone will continue to grow.

“Furthermore, if we don’t qualify, we will fail to achieve an vital objective: so that’s why we have to start the match differently than Benfica and Ferencváros. We’ll see.”.

What can you tell us about Cisse as a striker?

In a recent development, “I think he can play very well in that role, in that position. Tonight I chose Cissé to play in that position and not Camarda because against Frosinone, one-on-one, Cissé has these characteristics more. Tonight the goal wasn’t to keep possession, but to run and attack the space.

Sources indicate that “Cissé is better at this than Camarda. We wanted to make more transitions than Frosinone, so it was a choice dictated by the player’s characteristics, but I think Cissé is good both as an attacking midfielder and as a central striker, and not just as a winger.”.

Bristol City vs Wrexham - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (717 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Adepoju Marvellous | 23 Nov 2026 16:55, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 12:37.
  • Matchday 17 of the 2026-27 Championship season sees struggling Bristol City host high-flying Wrexham at Ashton Gate on Tuesday evening.
  • The home side enter the clash on a run of three consecutive defeats, while Wrexham arrive unbeaten in their last three matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 23 Nov 2026 16:55, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 12:37.

Matchday 17 of the 2026-27 Championship season sees struggling Bristol City host high-flying Wrexham at Ashton Gate on Tuesday evening.

The home side enter the clash on a run of three consecutive defeats, while Wrexham arrive unbeaten in their last three matches.

Having guided Lincoln City to last season’s League One title with a remarkable 101 points, 12 clear of Cardiff City, Michael Skubala arrived at Bristol City full of confidence, but his start to life at Ashton Gate has been far from ideal.

Saturday’s 2-0 loss to Middlesbrough was an improvement on the 5-0 thrashing by Norwich City a fortnight earlier. Still, it was another disappointing result for the Robins, who have now won just one of their last eight league matches since returning from the September international break (D2, L5).

According to recent reports, with his side presently 18th in the Championship table, Skubala’s quest for back-to-back promotions has become increasingly challenging. However, the 44-year-old oversaw a 28-game unbeaten run last season to secure Lincoln the title and now hopes to engineer a similar turnaround at Bristol City.

Unbeaten in 12 of the last 13 meetings between the sides, Bristol City have enjoyed the upper hand in this fixture as Skubala aims to get the better of his opposite number for the first time in three managerial encounters, having lost the previous two by a combined score of 3-0.

In a recent development, after the Wrexham clash, Tuesday’s hosts face three promotion hopefuls - West Brom, Swansea City, and West Ham United - over the next four gameweeks. They will need to raise their level to avoid anxiously looking over their shoulder at the bottom three as the hectic festive period approaches.

Wrexham narrowly missed out on a playoff spot last season and were tipped as promotion contenders this term, but after securing just three wins from their opening 13 matches, those expectations were swiftly dampened.

Off the back of consecutive defeats to Blackburn Rovers and Sheffield United to close out October, Phil Parkinson’s men have started November with wins over Middlesbrough and, most recently, Lincoln - either side of a 1-1 draw with Wolverhampton Wanderers.

The Red Dragons’ tally of seven points from the last nine available is the joint third-best in the Championship, so they should travel to a ground where they have never previously won in confident mood.

With just six goals in their eight away league matches so far, Wrexham could do with greater attacking impetus as they seek back-to-back victories on the road for the first time since a four-match winning run at the start of January.

Having conceded 30% of their 20 goals in the final 15 minutes of matches, Tuesday’s visitors must address their late-game struggles, particularly against opponents who have scored nearly half of their 16 goals in that period.

Bristol City Championship form:.

Twenty-four-year-old Noah Eile has not featured since September 18 and remains Bristol City’s only fitness concern ahead of Tuesday’s game.

Scott Twine, who has scored four of the hosts’ last seven goals, is expected to return to the starting lineup after being limited to a 30-minute cameo against Middlesbrough last time out.

Liberato Cacace (calf) and Sam Smith (knee) are confirmed absentees for Wrexham, with Cacace still awaiting his first appearance of the 2026-27 season.

Nathan Broadhead (thigh), Seb Revan (hamstring), and Josh Windass (ankle) are major doubts for the visitors, who are also monitoring the fitness of Callum O’Hare.

Kieffer Moore remains his side’s leading scorer with five goals, but has failed to find the net in his last five appearances.

Bristol City possible starting lineup:.

Collins; Pring, Atkinson, Dickie, Tanner; Randell, Kinght; Twine, De Keersmaecker, Cardines; Tolaj.

Wrexham possible starting lineup:.

Patterson; Doyle, Worrall, Cleworth; Ekomie, Whiteman, Sheaf, Kabore; Thomason, O’Brien; Moore.

Wrexham are the more confident of the two teams, and while Bristol City have struggled to make home advantage count lately, losing four in a row at Ashton Gate, they cannot be counted out.

We anticipate an open, end-to-end contest, with the hosts narrowly emerging victorious to relieve some of the pressure on Skubala.

#95160. How to make AI data centres more sustainable

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1283 w)

How to make AI data centres more sustainable

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1283 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, AI companies must engage with those who oppose the expansion of data centres.Credit: Michael M.
  • In a recent development, around the world, people are demanding a halt to the proliferation of data centres — racks of computers, housed in warehouses, that are powering the boom in artificial intelligence.
  • Recent findings suggest that is the climate totally cooked?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, AI companies must engage with those who oppose the expansion of data centres.Credit: Michael M. Santiago/Getty.

In a recent development, around the world, people are demanding a halt to the proliferation of data centres — racks of computers, housed in warehouses, that are powering the boom in artificial intelligence. Communities worry that existing infrastructure will not be able to handle the surge in demand for electricity and water, and that data centres’ energy demands will cause environmental and health problems, including increases in air pollution and greenhouse-gas emissions. The question of whether AI is going to stall climate action is explored in the first of a three-part Nature Podcast (Nature https://doi.org/rzqs; 2026).

Is the climate totally cooked? What the data say.

Recent findings suggest that is the climate totally cooked? What the data say.

People have many concerns about the way AI is being developed, including how it might affect safety, security and jobs. Where energy is concerned, however, any added demand for computing power can, and must, be met in smart, sustainable ways, not by burning more fossil fuels. Achieving this will take some creative thinking, and researchers need to be closely involved. Many argue that there are alternatives to relying on energy-intensive data centres, such as AI models that can run on individual computers or institutional servers, thereby consuming much less power than those run using cloud services. Efforts to develop such options need to be better funded.

According to recent reports, future projections of data centres’ energy demands are hard to make, because they are based on assumptions that could change. If current global trends continue, electricity consumption by data centres will go on rising. Between 2017 and 2024, it grew by around 12% per year. Figures for 2024 from the International Energy Agency (IEA), based in Paris, show most of this demand coming from three regions: the United States (45%), China (25%) and Europe (15%).

The Electric Power Research Institute, a non-profit organization in Palo Alto, California, has projected that the continued growth of US data centres could add up to 94 gigawatts of demand by 2030, equivalent to 17% of the country’s electricity consumption. Data centres right now consume more than 1.5% of the world’s electricity supply, and the IEA’s projections indicate that this figure will more than double in the next few years. By 2030, data centres could consume more electricity than Japan, the agency says.

Why scientists should lead the shift away from AI mega data centres.

Why scientists should lead the shift away from AI mega data centres.

There are serious concerns that this extra demand will be powered mainly by fossil fuels, when carbon emissions are already at a record high. Research published this week in Nature Sustainability estimates that some 400 data centres in the United States accounted for around 26 megatonnes of carbon dioxide emissions between May 2024 and April 2025, more than those produced by many countries (G. Guidi et al. Nature Sustain. https://doi.org/hcsptc; 2026). And according to a study published last week in Nature Climate Change, data centres’ energy demands could prolong the lifespan of coal-fired power stations (C. Li et al. Nature Clim. Change https://doi.org/rzqr; 2026).

According to recent reports, but none of this is inevitable. Governments could mandate that new energy demand be met with renewable sources. And regulators could look at alternative ways to manage existing electric supplies.

Many nations’ electric grid systems are designed to accommodate surges in demand, whether to power extra cooling on hot summer days or extra heating during winter cold snaps. Much of the time, there is excess capacity. This excess could be used to reduce the amount of fresh energy needed to power data centres.

Sources indicate that how much energy will AI really consume? The good, the bad and the unknown.

How much energy will AI really consume? The good, the bad and the unknown.

One solution is to curtail data-centre operations during periods of peak electricity consumption, and ramp up at times of lower demand. An analysis released in 2025 by researchers at Duke University in Durham, North Carolina, found that the US electric grid could accommodate 98 gigawatts of extra demand in this way, without adding any new generation capacity (see go.nature.com/4cdeknm). That 98 gigawatts would be enough to cover most, if not all, of the expected expansion in US data centres over the next few years.

There is potential for this to become a reality. In June, as part of a larger effort to modernize the grid, the US Federal Energy Regulatory Commission instructed grid operators to draw up a blueprint for how they will cope with extra demand from data centres. The technology industry is understandably paying close attention to how it might mitigate the problems of powering data centres. Earlier this month, OpenAI unveiled what it is calling a “grid protectors program”, a project to consult with US grid operators, regulators and policymakers to see how the organization can work around peaks in power demand.

Meanwhile, Google is paying households and businesses in parts of the Eastern United States to reduce their electricity consumption during periods of high demand. Similar proposals are being considered in other countries.

Why open-source generative AI models are an ethical way forward for science.

Why open-source generative AI models are an ethical way forward for science.

Sources indicate that these are all tentative moves in the right direction, although arguably progress is not being made fast enough. Policymakers and data-centre operators must engage seriously with those who oppose the centres’ expansion. At a minimum, any new energy sources developed to power these centres must be renewable. Existing energy sources can also be better deployed, and researchers working to develop alternatives to energy-intensive data centres should be better supported. More peer-reviewed evidence is needed, especially for countries outside the United States.

Industry observers note that there are smarter and more sustainable ways to power the growth of AI, but to achieve them, concerted and coordinated action will be needed. In this way, the harm posed to people and the planet can be minimized, and AI technologies can benefit everyone.

#95158. Hull reignite genuine survival hopes with late Oli McBurnie double to down Brighton, as talk of Seagulls emulating Leicester City-style fairytale is made to look foolish

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (884 w)

Hull reignite genuine survival hopes with late Oli McBurnie double to down Brighton, as talk of Seagulls emulating Leicester City-style fairytale is made to look foolish

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (884 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:04 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:08 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • When Brighton owner Tony Bloom was asked about his club’s title prospects last week, he suggested they could emulate Leicester City’s 2015-16 fairytale and win the Premier League.
  • It was a bold claim, yet Fabian Hurzeler’s men looked anything but title aspirants after being downed by Oli McBurnie’s dramatic late double for newly-promoted Hull City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:04 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:08 EST, 23 November 2026.

When Brighton owner Tony Bloom was asked about his club’s title prospects last week, he suggested they could emulate Leicester City’s 2015-16 fairytale and win the Premier League.

It was a bold claim, yet Fabian Hurzeler’s men looked anything but title aspirants after being downed by Oli McBurnie’s dramatic late double for newly-promoted Hull City.

Brighton have been the most credible challengers to Arsenal so far this season. That cannot be denied.

With Manchester City wobbling alarmingly, and the rest of the traditional significant guns largely off the title pace, the Seagulls have at least given Mikel Arteta’s champions something to think about.

But this bitterly cold afternoon in East Yorkshire was a reality check for Hurzeler’s men and a harsh lesson in taking the chances that come your way.

Brighton didn’t and McBurnie most certainly did, firing home clinically from close range twice in added time shortly after Joao Costinha had been sent off.

Oli McBurnie scored a late brace to secure a brilliant three points for Hull against Brighton.

McBurnie has made a habit of leaving it late – the rejuvenated Scotland striker struck a 95th-minute winner in the Championship play-off final against Middlesbrough at Wembley in May.

Hull had gone eight Premier League games without a win before Brighton’s visit and this success lifted them to 11th.

Tigers boss Sergej Jakirovic said of McBurnie: 'I’ve never had any doubts over a ‘Braveheart’ like Oli because he’s a natural leader and very important for us.'.

Asked where the setback left Brighton’s title hopes, Hurzeler remarked: 'We don’t focus on the table – we focus on performances and how we can make the right improvements into the team.

'That’s the same if we had won or lost, but today demonstrated there are still things we need to do better. That’s what we will do and then see what the outcome will be.'.

Brighton arrived as favourites and could have cut Arsenal's lead at the top of the table.

Hull were indebted to a remarkable display from their Greek goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, who reduced Brighton to an afternoon of frustration and futility.

The visitors had 10 attempts at goal during the first half alone, forcing Hull’s summer signing into a string of fine saves and also being denied by the woodwork.

At times the Seagulls’ pretty patterns threatened to cut the Tigers apart as the likes of Maxim De Cuyper, Diego Gomez and the effervescent Pascal Gross – on his 300th appearance for the club – knitted them together superbly.

Georginio Rutter was involved in a move which saw De Cuyper cross low from the left flank to the onrushing Gomez, whose close-range effort was superbly saved by Tzolakis.

That set the tone for an outstanding display by the 24-year-old Greece international, who arrived in the summer from Olympiacos as part of the newly-promoted Tigers’ £150million spending spree which saw 18 players signed.

Hull lacked nothing in spirit and fight but Brighton had the quality and constantly threatened to open up their hosts.

As half-time approached, Rutter saw a close-range shot repelled by Tzolakis after Yasin Ayari’s effort rebounded off the crossbar.

The Tigers were constantly grateful to their goalkeeper, who made another save to keep out an effort from Gomez on the stroke of half-time.

Tzolakis continued to prove unbeatable in the second half too, and his opposite number Bart Verbruggen was left grateful to the woodwork after a cross-shot from substitute Sorba Thomas hit the crossbar.

Mohamed Belloumi was also a lingering threat for Hull on the right flank and he should have scored after cutting infield before firing wastefully wide.

Konstantinos Tzolakis (right) produced a remarkable display to keep Brighton out.

As the game wore on, there was an inescapable feeling that Brighton could be punished for their wastefulness as Hull revealed the kind of courage which deserves, and usually gets, its rewards.

Regan Slater cleared a shot from Charalampos Kostoulas off the line before Brighton lost Joao Costinha to a second yellow card with a minute remaining.

The Tigers sensed blood, pouring forward to lead in the first minute of added time as McBurnie expertly sidefooted them in front from Lucas Gourna-Douath’s neat pass to cap a delightful flowing move.

Industry observers note that moments before the final whistle, Hull struck again as McBurnie swept home from close range again from Mo Belloumi’s assist. Cue delirium in the home stands.

McBurnie took the acclaim but Tzolakis was Hull’s star man as Jakirovic acknowledged: 'Tzolakis was amazing and we could have been two or three-nil down without his saves.

Sources indicate that 'We stayed alive because of him and then won the game at the end. Ciao!'.

Hull had failed to win since beating Manchester United and Coventry in their opening two games in August.

Hull reignited their survival hopes with a precious win against an in-form team.

Crucially, however, they have been competitive in every game this season and are now unbeaten in six home matches.

Can they survive? 'Of course, and every win is so vital,' declared Jakirovic.

'I wish this feeling I have now would never stop but I know how demanding this league is.'.

Hurzeler could certainly attest to that.

Paris Saint-Germain vs Roma - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 23 Nov 2026 17:21, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43.
  • Double Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain will look to continue their stroll through this season's league phase, when they welcome Roma to Parc des Princes on Wednesday evening.
  • The competition's top scorers, peerless PSG have claimed maximum points, while their Italian visitors have spectacularly thrown several away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 23 Nov 2026 17:21, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43.

Double Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain will look to continue their stroll through this season's league phase, when they welcome Roma to Parc des Princes on Wednesday evening.

The competition's top scorers, peerless PSG have claimed maximum points, while their Italian visitors have spectacularly thrown several away.

Having kicked off their second title defence with an emphatic 6-1 win over Slovan Bratislava, PSG then posted consecutive 4-2 victories against Manchester City and Barcelona.

Usually sluggish starters in the league phase, Luis Enrique's men then stepped up another gear by smashing six past Villarreal without reply, ruthlessly maintaining their perfect record.

Already out of sight within 16 minutes and two seconds, PSG set a new fastest time to score four goals in a Champions League match, before slightly easing off the gas.

Furthermore, a tally of 20 goals is the most by any club from their first four group or league phase fixtures, and Barca's overall best of 28 is now under serious threat.

Also unbeaten in 14 games at Europe's elite level, Les Parisiens can surpass Lyon's French record by at least avoiding defeat in midweek.

Despite losing Desire Doue to a serious injury, PSG still beat Nice 3-2 on Saturday night, recording their 12th consecutive win across all competitions.

Now leading city rivals Paris FC by three points at the top of the Ligue 1 table, they are well set to sweep all before them again.

Ahead of their first competitive meeting with PSG - a prospect to be feared and savoured in equal measure - Roma warmed up with a 5-1 win over Parma at the weekend.

Staying within two points of surprise Serie A leaders Lazio - their loathed city rivals - the Giallorossi inched ahead of Scudetto holders Inter Milan, largely thanks to a four-goal haul for Donyell Malen.

After another stellar display at Stadio Tardini, Malen has racked up 26 league goals in 2026, while Roma have already fired home 36 this season.

That is more than any other team at this stage of an Italian top-flight campaign since 1950, and Gian Piero Gasperini's side also remain unbeaten.

However, in the Champions League they have effectively let eight points slip, following a late collapse at home to Real Madrid and their massive blow-up at Old Trafford earlier this month.

Roma somehow squandered a two-goal lead to lose against Manchester United on matchday four, leaving them 20th in the Champions League standings and at risk of early elimination.

Now bound for France to face the toughest test of all, the Giallorossi have won just one of their last 11 away games in UEFA's top competition, while conceding in all of the last 33.

Paris Saint-Germain Champions League form:.

Paris Saint-Germain form (all competitions):.

Further diminishing PSG's talented front line, Doue must join Khvicha Kvaratskhelia on the long road to recovery from an ACL injury.

More positively for Luis Enrique - a former Roma coach - Ousmane Dembele recently made his comeback from a layoff.

Fabian Ruiz has posted goal involvements in all of his last four Champions League appearances, scoring in the last two, and he should start in central midfield.

Club captain Marquinhos moved to Paris from Roma in 2013, while reserve left-back Lucas Digne spent the 2015-16 campaign on loan with the Giallorossi.

Roma welcomed back Paulo Dybala and first-choice goalkeeper Mile Svilar during the international break, but Lorenzo Pellegrini is still unavailable.

Devyne Rensch (adductor) and Leonardo Balerdi (ankle) are both struggling to recover in time for Wednesday's game.

Brazilian wing-back Wesley notched a hat-trick of assists in Parma, despite only appearing as a second-half substitute, so he will expect to play at Parc des Princes.

A sure starter up front, Malen now tops the Capocannoniere rankings with 12 Serie A goals, having recently scored in the Nations League and found the net in three consecutive Champions League matches.

Paris Saint-Germain possible starting lineup:.

Safonov; Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes; Zaire-Emery, Vitinha, Ruiz; Akliouche, Dembele, Mayulu.

Svilar; Mancini, Ndicka, Hermoso; Molina, Cristante, Kone, Wesley; Soule, Mora; Malen.

PSG's latest injury setback will surely have an impact, but the goals and points should keep flowing on Wednesday.

While Gasperini's Roma are often a delight to behold, their defence can be caught out at the very top level, so they will leave Paris empty-handed.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • By the end of an extraordinary evening in Madrid, where United went 1-0 down inside a minute and never recovered against Atlético Madrid, Martínez had blown the lid off any pretence of all being well at the club as he launched a lacerating assault on the club’s executives.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, michael Carrick had urged his Manchester United players to come out and fight. But nobody could have imagined quite how Lisandro Martínez would interpret that message.

By the end of an extraordinary evening in Madrid, where United went 1-0 down inside a minute and never recovered against Atlético Madrid, Martínez had blown the lid off any pretence of all being well at the club as he launched a lacerating assault on the club’s executives.

United had come into this getting battered from all sides and when Pablo Barrios put Atlético ahead, Jamie Carragher’s pre-match assessment about how things could get “very messy, very promptly” for all involved at Old Trafford must have been ringing in the ears of the travelling supporters.

ATLETICO ARE AHEAD IN JUST 53 SECONDS! ⚡️ A nightmare start for United at the Metropolitano Stadium 😬 https://t.co/TdOwoXxopn.

They certainly know how to make life difficult for themselves. Leny Yoro’s 74th-minute red card pretty much ended hopes of them taking something from the game.

Industry observers note that ademola Lookman scored Atlético’s second soon after and Carrick was staring at another defeat. And so they now move on to a substantial game at Leeds on Sunday. This was not the result Carrick would have wanted – and that is before what happened off the pitch.

Ademola Lookman PUNISHES a 10-man Man United 💥 https://t.co/GHKYIHGhNC.

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

Industry observers note that on the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30.

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

According to recent reports, martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

No one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring challenges to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

It has been revealed that having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the firm man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

It now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

That Martínez picked this game to speak out was interesting. United, lost, yes, and the manner of Atlético’s opening goal from Barrios after 53 seconds was shocking. But United at least went down fighting on this occasion and had fashioned enough good chances to at least draw level before Yoro’s harsh 74th-minute red card swung a delicately poised match decisively in Atlético’s favour.

Lookman made it 2-0 soon after, but Atlético, having looked like they would run all over United in those opening 10 minutes, were made to work hard for their victory.

United cannot keep shooting themselves in the foot like they did in the first minute. Carrick had gone with a three-man midfield to shore things up and made his team more comfortable and yet they were opened up in double quick time by two passes through the middle.

Still, you only needed to look across at United’s opponents to appreciate how chaotic it had become at Old Trafford.

Diego Simeone’s reign at Atlético covers a period stretching two years longer than the post-Ferguson era and in many ways his teams have represented everything United have not been in that time: well constructed and thought through, unified, stable, organised, hungry, aggressive, uncompromising and with a flash of devilment.

If United were not in crisis before this, they are now.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30.

It’s a fresh night and we’ve got to adapt, we’ve got to adjust in a positive way.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Atlético Madrid and Manchester United from the Metropolitano. The two sides had contrasting fortunes in their opening fixtures in this competition, Man Utd beating Azerbaijan’s Sabah 4-0 at Old Trafford a month ago while Atléti were defeated by Liverpool who came back from 1-0 down to win 2-1.

But domestically it is the other way round – Michael Carrick’s side have made the club’s worst start in the league for 40 years with one win, three draws and two defeats and have been knocked out of the League Cup. Those of us who watch them regularly – purely because of occupational obligations in this instance – have been surprised by how poor they have been. The results have been bad but the performances even worse.

They seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

Atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

Simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

Industry observers note that the one surviving veteran in the squad from that first of El Cholo’s Liga winning sides and the two Champions League finals, victory in which would represent Simeone’s crowning achievement, is the midfielder Koke. Remarkably, if he features today, the 34-year-old midfielder will be making his 750th first-team appearance as an Atlético player.

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 11:10 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:10 EST, 23 November 2026.

Footage has emerged of Ange Postecoglou locked in a fiery exchange with a reporter after Al-Nassr's defeat to Al-Ahli - after he questioned Sadio Mane's commitment to the Saudi Pro League club.

The side sits third in the league standings, but were humbled in the 3-1 loss to their fourth-placed rivals on the road.

Mane was not named in the matchday squad despite registering two assists in the club's last outing, a 6-2 victory against Asian Champions League opponents Pakhtakor FC.

One Saudi journalist is believed to have used Mane's absence to suggest that he was not sufficiently engaged with Al-Nassr's campaign this season.

But even the suggestion was enough to incense the former Tottenham head coach, who immediately asked if the journalist was 'a father?'.

'Do you have children?' he queried, with the journalist responding that he did not.

Ange Postecoglou snapped at the journalist who questioned the strength of Sadio Mane's commitment to Al-Nassr.

Should footballers ever be criticised for choosing family over club commitments?

The Senegal forward missed the match as he and his wife await the birth of their second child.

It has been revealed that 'That's probably why you ask the question,' Postecoglou hit back. 'Because when you do, you'll realise it's the most key thing, the biggest blessing you can have.

'(Mane) is with his wife while she is having a baby, OK? Nothing is more vital in life.

'Yes, he had my permission, my blessing, and Sadio Mane is one of the best people in this world, mate.

'Never question him or his commitment to this football club.'.

Mane welcomed his first child with wife Aisha Timba last year, after marrying the then-18-year-old in January 2024.

In his first match following the happy news, Mane scored and celebrated by rocking an imaginary baby in his arms.

Postecoglou and Mane have only worked with one another since the beginning of the season, but appear to have formed a strong bond with Mane a frequent starter in the Riyadh-based starting XI.

The Antipodean manager joined the club following a spell without work after his ignominious departure from Nottingham Forest last season.

Since arriving in the Gulf state, Postecoglou has overseen a strong domestic campaign, with Al-Nassr registering just one previous defeat this season, against Al-Ettifaq.

But Friday's loss may have stung all the more after Al-Nassr initially led against their bitter rivals.

Cristiano Ronaldo had opened the scoring for the visitors on Friday evening in Jeddah, but missed a penalty striking the far post and failed to double his side's lead.

Instead, it was Ivan Toney who was nerveless from the spot as he netted to put Al-Ahli 2-1 up in the 71st minute, with Roger Ibanez providing the winner four minutes later.

Heath were hoping to extend their good run of just one defeat in 12 matches, while the Us were hoping to get back to winning ways to aid their push for promotion.

Chris Simmons’ Heath took the lead on 12 minutes when Zac Young received the ball wide on the right some 40 yards from goal and the Heath talisman advanced towards the Hastings goal before striking a left-foot shot from distance that beat Us goalkeeper Harry Haines at the near post.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The visitors best chance of the half came five minutes before the break when Sam Pidgeon worked his way to the edge of the Heath penalty area and hit a left foot shot which deflected off the Heath goalkeeper Alfie Hadfield and flew narrowly wide of the post – but it remained 1-0 a the break.

The Us started the second half well, forcing Heath on to the backfoot but failing to create any clear-cut chances.

Their most dangerous tactic seemed to be launching long throws into the Bears penalty area where they met by a solid-looking Broadbridge Heath defence marshalled by Lewis Hyde and supported by his protégé Jay Richardson.

But the Bears doubled their lead on the hour mark when Young received the ball wide on the right of the Hastings penalty area and forced his way forward, where he was challenged by a defender – bringing the Heath player crashing to the ground.

The match referee had no doubt about it being a foul, pointing immediately to the penalty spot, and MoM Young picked himself up, dusted himself down and hammered the spot kick into the back of the net for his second of the afternoon, helping his side to a 2-0 win.

The victory saw Broadbridge Heath move into one of the play-off places in seventh – just one point behind Hastings United.

Fixtures continue to come thick and fast with the Bears travelling to second-placed Erith Town on Tuesday evening before returning home again on Saturday to face leaders Faversham Town.

BBH: Hadfield, Thiselton, Royall, Marino (Church 65), Hyde (Peters 70), Richardson, Connell, Bejashvili (Rawlins 71), Buchanan, Hards (Doughty 90), Young.

Roffey faced clear table toppers Haywards Heath, at the Fusion Aviation Stadium on Saturday, determined to gain revenge for the narrow, and perhaps undeserved, loss at Hanbury Park earlier in the season. However, in the end, despite having 14 attempts on goal with 6 on target, it was the visitors who took the points with two clinical finishes from their four on target efforts and two off target.

According to recent reports, in the second minute Jordan Mase went down the left then cut in and switched the ball across the box to Luke Harrison whose shot took a slight deflection, taking the pace off it and Ethan McGrath in the Blues goal saved. In the fourth minute Mase again advanced before squaring it, this time to Stan Berry who hit a fierce drive just past the right-hand post, with McGrath probably covering it. Two minutes later Tom Caplin fed Moyo on the right and after his first cross was blocked at the near post he found Caplin 12 yards out but his shot although right in the corner, lacked the pace to beat McGrath.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

In a recent development, the Boars continued to dominate possession and after a quarter of an hour, Mase set the ball back for Charlie Gibson to fire over from twenty yards. Next a Gibson corner was deflected up in the air by a defender and Pat Gibs headed it back into the danger area where Berry controlled the ball in the air before hitting a spectacular bicycle shot a foot over the bar. Gibson hit his hot wide at the end of quick break and Berry hit the side netting after good work from Harrison and Callum Kilkenny.

Recent findings suggest that heath had their first attempt on goal after twenty-two minutes when Sonny Causton was played through, but with defenders converging, hit his shot from the edge of the box straight at Charlie Burton. Back came Roffey and Teddy Wood put a twenty yarder narrowly past the right-hand post. Heath responded with Mark Goldson getting behind the defence, but Pat Gibbs held him up and the Boars got men back with his attempt ending tamely in Burton’s arms. Goldson had another chance when the ball was switched from the right, but he sliced his shot wide.

The breakthrough came on thirty-three minutes when a Roffey attack broke down, and the ball was quickly transferred to Josh Wright who had kept himself onside. Burton advanced to push him wide but Callum Kilkenny who had sprinted back went over the top of the outstretched keeper and Wright managed to squeeze the ball in at the far post despite the desperate efforts of Jack Meeres on the line. Wood replied with a shot that was saved comfortably by McGrath. After all that action the half ended quietly with the visitors having the advantage.

Recent findings suggest that roffey had the first attempt on goal after the break with Moyo’s shot being taken above his head by McGrath. The game became much more contained with Heath happy to close Roffey down and maintain their lead. The next significant action didn’t come until thirteen minutes before time when Roffey lost possession in their own area but forced Harry Shooman to shoot over. Roffey were still very much in the game, but this changed on eighty minutes as they threw men forward, the hosts were caught on the break and Wright held off Meeres and rolled the ball past Burton to double the lead. Roffey wouldn’t give up but Heath were now able to sit back and soak up the pressure. Gibsons free kick hit the wall and deflected for a corner which was cleared. As stoppage time approached the Boars had a great chance to stay in the game when Caplin spread the play out to Harrison whose cross picked out the same player, unmarked ten yards out, but he scuffed his shot and McGrath saved. There was still time for Moyo to force a save out of McGrath at the near post and the same player hit a shot wide but unfortunately time had run out for the Boars. The table toppers had shown a clinical edge and managed their way to the three points.

Roffey are still very much in the fight for a top five place and it looks like that could be between eight or nine teams and the Boars next match is away to one of them, Hassocks who sit two places above the Boars, on December 1st.

Roffey: Burton, Harrison, Gibson, Napper, Gibbs(Moyo), Meeres, Wood, Mase, Berry(Allen), Caplin, Kilkenny(Hoarty). Subs: Pearse, Skerry.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Martin O’Neill believes Kieran Tierney is back to his very best and harbours no fears about the defender’s fitness levels ahead of a frantic festive schedule.

Although the Celtic manager substituted Tierney towards the end of Saturday’s 4-1 win over St Mirren, the player started – and finished – both of Scotland’s games in the recent international window, when he was deployed as left centre-half in a back-three formation favoured by latest international manager Sebastien Pocognoli.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

O’Neill admits this could be an option for Celtic if he chooses to play a system that he once was synonymous with during his first spell in charge at the club.

According to recent reports, “Kieran can play as a centre-half, there’s no doubt about it,” said O’Neill. “He competes better in the air than I ever thought he did.

“It was only when I came back to Celtic that I realised that. He will battle in the air and he’s a reliable defender. If we are ever dropping into a back three, then it wouldn’t be a problem for him.”.

Celtic face a tough upcoming run of games, including travelling to take on second-tier Portuguese club Torreense in the Europa League on Thursday night. Two more away games against Hearts and Dundee promptly follow. The Parkhead side have just one more home match – against St Johnstone – before Christmas. Two other assignments, against Aberdeen and Omonia Nicosia, are away.

O’Neill has already spoken of “manoeuvring” players in the first-team squad to ensure no one is pushed beyond their limits.

Recent findings suggest that tierney clearly merits the most concern given his injury history. However, he has been quietly putting in the minutes for his club as well as his country in recent weeks. He has played the full 90 minutes of two of Celtic’s last four matches and was only subbed off on Saturday with 20 minutes left against St Mirren with the game already won. O’Neill revealed that he has a crafty tactic for dealing with the player if he begins to look like he might want to come off; he pretends not to notice him. There is no point in the player looking forlornly towards the dugout.

“Tierney played two 90 minutes for Scotland and that made it difficult for him to last the full game against St Mirren,” said O'Neill.

“Internationals take it out of you and he played every second. He played left centre back and that maybe means less running, but those games are tough.

“Previous to his injury, he was feeling it. But since he’s been back, he’s played a lot of games. Sometimes with Kieran, when you feel as if he’s flagging, you just ignore him. If he’s coming near you, you turn away because you want him to play the games!

“Kieran has done great for me,” he added. "He’s been brilliant, he really has, and he’s getting fitter too. Kieran will be significant for us in Europe again. You look at the Besiktas game. Our winning goal late on came from his shot when he was still getting high up the pitch.

“Kieran has done so well for us and there are signs that he’s back to the Kieran Tierney who got a move to Arsenal. He defends well, he creates goals and he comes up with some too.

Industry observers note that “I genuinely couldn’t speak highly enough about Kieran. He’s a great lad too - very popular in the dressing room.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 4-1 defeat left Guernsey smarting and United in a very good position in second place in the SCFL Premier.

Industry observers note that since then, the Green Lions have been on an unbeaten run, making themselves genuine play-off contenders along with United. It was obvious from the moment they arrived at the Oval that they would only be happy with all three points, preferably by at least the same scoreline.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The early encounters went to United, and with just seven minutes on the clock James Jull shot home, only for the linesman to raise his flag for offside to howls of derision from the home support.

Guernsey started to make their mark with a couple of runs from Charlton Gauvain, but the visitors also left their mark on United’s players, collecting two yellow cards.

Hull went very close with an acrobatic scissor kick, and Joe Overy continued to needle away down the left wing, Charlie Ball forcing the keeper into a good save from one of Overy’s low crosses.

In first half added time, Guernsey took the lead with a fine shot from range beating Alieu Secka.

United were unperturbed and Rhyle Ovenden was unfortunate not to even it up straight after the break, his free kick just scraping the top of the crossbar.

On the hour Hull was replaced by Callum Barlow, before the increasingly confident Ovenden had a shot well saved by the Lions keeper.

Recent findings suggest that five minutes later, Barlow’s lightning-fast cross found Overy, who turned and slotted home well for 1-1. Overy rarely misses an attempt in the area, and Guernsey looked crestfallen.

There was a third and a fourth yellow card for Guernsey, who were pondering returning with only a point, when Ball broke past the defences and slotted home with an inch perfect side foot to make it 2-1 to United to the joy of the crowd, and despair of the islanders.

It has been revealed that rather than crumble, it galvanised Guernsey, and the United lead only lasted four minutes as Gauvain made it 2-2. Now it was a real blood and thunder contest, both teams showing exactly why they are in the top four, Secka made a wonderful save to keep it equal, Ball and Barlow both trying out the away keeper, but it remained 2-2.

After months out injured, the home crowd were delighted to see – on 85 minutes – Mason Creese come on, replacing Ball, and Freddie Jones took up position on the other flank replacing Overy.

Both added even more pace, and despite the cold, the crowd were heating up – while Guernsey overheated as they collected a fifth yellow in what was never a nasty encounter. As the final whistle went both teams were treated to an ovation as they left the field. This is the sort of fare non-league crowds absolutely love - hard tackling, fast attacking, stout defending and not a player from either side faking injury to get an opponent booked.

Both teams should be in the play-offs - one of them could be champions, time will tell.

Next up for United, this Saturday, is a home game with an improving Forest Row, who will be desperate for the points to help them out of the drop zone. It’s a 3pm kick-off at the Oval.

Adrien Rabiot heaped praise on Goncalo Ramos for what he does for the team, but he also explained what AC Milan’s ‘problem’ is.

Milan put on a show for their fans at San Siro on Sunday evening as they beat Frosinone 5-1. Gabriele Calvani’s own goal put the home side ahead, before Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netted to make it a rout.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that it is a third consecutive league victory after the wins over Inter and Genoa and it moves the Rossoneri on to 27 points, back inside the Champions League places. Up next: a trip to Athens to face Olympiacos on Thursday in the Europa League, and a chance to demonstrate consistency.

In a recent development, after the full-time whistle, Rabiot spoke alongside Ramos to both Sky and DAZN, offering his thoughts on what was a very successful evening in front of all the fans at San Siro. His words are via MilanNews.

Are you starting to build a good identity?

It has been revealed that “Our problem is that we have to be focused for 90 minutes. We did well today, even though we conceded a bit at the end, but that’s normal. As I said, we’re growing as a team: the quality of our play, the team spirit, the sacrifice for 90 minutes, and everyone.

“Gonçalo is the first to do a lot. Today I saw he had a bit of pain in his thigh. I know he’s a very notable player for us, and we have a lot of games: I even asked the coach to let him rest a bit. But everyone’s attitude was great today, and we have to keep it up.

Sources indicate that “In these last few games, when we play like this, when we’re so focused and manage to do what we work towards in training, I think we’re all enjoying ourselves, even tonight. We created a lot, we scored a lot of goals. What we have to focus on is enjoying playing together.”.

Why didn’t you shoot before the first goal?

Industry observers note that “I wanted Pulisic to score, but the defender came back quickly. It’s true that I could have shot, but I get more pleasure from providing an assist than from scoring. But I did the assist afterwards.”.

Recent findings suggest that “He does a great job. Not everyone understands it, but he does an incredible job. When we get in and score, it’s also credit to us. Then we feel happy when he scores, also because it gives him confidence. Good for us and for him, for everyone.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alfred Johansson insists Motherwell’s latest accounts show the club are trending upwards - with Norway’s Bodo Glimt a key reference point.

The Premiership side have reported a profit of £2.3M, which rises to £3.1M when excluding depreciation and finance costs, for the 2025/26 financial year. A record of £5M was generated from player trading while former manager Jens Berthel Askou achieved a fourth place finish in last term’s top flight.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Recent findings suggest that current manager Johansson’s work was largely in Scandinavia before travelling to Motherwell. He watched Bodo’s rise from lowly divisions to Champions League competitors and feels that reveals what a step-by-step approach can do for a club’s long term aspirations. Former Rosenborg gaffer Johansson said: “I can't really use that to ask for more time in terms of performing but definitely, it's evidence of what the club has been doing for the past 18 months at least, that it’s something that is working.

“So that alignment in the club, that philosophy, and that strategy, like we do things like this, and the connection I feel between people inside here and the offices, that everyone wants to pull together in that direction. That is what gives you output all the time.

Sources indicate that “This is a club that the budget is very small compared with some of the teams that we want to compete with. That was the same for Bodo/Glimt 10 years ago. Their budget was so small, they went down to the 2nd division in Norway, now they are playing Champions League. You have to build stone by stone, and that's what Motherwell are trying to do, and that's what I feel every day inside these walls.”.

It has been revealed that motherwell’s long-term goals are also set to be boosted by a training base being built at nearby Dalziel Park where they right now undergo preparation for matches. Johansson is keen to see the club build on its ability to grasp marginal gains. He explained: ”You don't have that much time in football nowadays. I get asked in the press conference about patience and everything is related to time.

According to recent reports, “That means that you have to make the most out of your time. Maybe before 30 years ago you had to optimise every week. Now you have to optimise every hour in top football. That's down to recovery of players, work with their bodies, and you need facilities to be able to facilitate that work. So that's one part of it.

In a recent development, “That you need to add the facilities for the players to be able to do the work that's needed to play every few days and with that intensity that. Now I saw that from all the top leagues in Europe, that the Scottish Premiership was the second in the world in explosive accelerations, for instance.

It has been revealed that “That's one of the more demanding things that you can put the body through. So you need to be able to react. You need to recover from that between matches and trainings, and so on. So you need the facilities for that. We don't have that much time. Right now we are driving back and forth to Dalziel Park. I could maybe take five minutes in my office with a player or on the pitch talking to a player. All of this is optimising time and I think it's essential today.”.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley spoke last week of the lack of national performance centre in Scotland, like Sweden are building in Johansson’s homeland. He added: “I definitely see the point of that's needed. I mean, Denmark, they've been working also now for some years.

“They have a plan now in place for how to build that centre, Sweden the same. Uh, we know that other countries, they did it 20 years ago, like like the Belgians and the Portuguese FA, they did it. They built a new facility after the Euros. So, of course, it's there to push things and it's needed.”.

Chema Andres insists Brighton will bounce back from their Premier League defeat at Hull City as the Seagulls turn their attention to Thursday's European test at the Amex Stadium.

Fabian Hurzeler's side - who remain second in the table - suffered a 2-0 loss at the MKM Stadium on Sunday, with Oli McBurnie scoring twice in stoppage time after Albion missed chances to take control.

Brighton were frustrated after failing to make their first-half dominance count, but midfielder Andres is looking ahead to the visit of Romanian league leaders Universitatea Craiova in the Uefa Conference League.

The Spaniard has made an impressive impact since his £18m summer arrival, featuring 10 times for Albion in all competitions, including eight Premier League appearances. He has also scored and provided an assist.

Andres believes the squad must learn from the setback at Hull rather than allow it to affect their confidence.

“What is good for us, we have another game on Thursday,” he said.

“We're already focused on that, and I think we need to focus on ourselves, keep training, see what we did wrong today, learn, and of course go again because this is football and sometimes you lose.

“I think the team spirit and team effort is not going to go down, so we will come back again.”.

The 21-year-old acknowledged the cost of Brighton's missed chances against a Hull side who showed their quality late on.

“This is the Premier League, no? If you don't use the chances you have, and then you give this kind of team the opportunity to beat you, that is what they got.”.

Andres added that Albion must accept the defeat, learn from it and move forward quickly.

Thursday's meeting with Craiova offers an immediate opportunity for Brighton to respond.

“We will recover from this and bounce back again,” he said.

Brighton then return to Premier League action this Sunday against Newcastle at the Amex Stadium.

Celtic’s historic European dream hinges on remaining unbeaten in their next two Europa League ties in Portugal and Cyprus as they seek to build on the win over Besiktas before the international break.

This, at least, is manager Martin O'Neill's view ahead of Thursday night's clash against Torreense, who have already amassed twice as many points as Celtic. The Portuguese second-tier side might be the most likely source of the win O'Neill feels is required. He has challenged his team to secure four points from the next two away fixtures.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

In a recent development, the 3-2 win over Besiktas earlier this month breathed some life back into the Parkhead club’s European campaign. "It gives us a chance, you know," said O'Neill.

Celtic are currently sitting 32nd out of 36 teams in the standings. They will have to break upcoming ground to finish among the top 24 and secure a place in the knockout stage. No team has managed to do so after opening with three defeats in the new European league format.

After Torreense in Leiria on Thursday Celtic travel to meet Omonia Nicosia in their final European game before Christmas. They play Marseille and Union St. Gilloise early in the newly introduced year.

Recent findings suggest that “You'd have to think that we'd need to get four points in the two games to give ourselves a chance so that you've got two left over, including a home game, which will not be easy," noted O'Neill. "It would be nice to carry it into January and still have a chance.

"We've taken enough criticism for not doing well enough in Europe and rightly so," he added. "It's the aim of the football club, it's what we've always remarked." O’Neill recalled a sponsors’ event last week where someone mentioned the manner of the Champions League qualifying exit. “Sometimes you feel as if we've never really got over the LASK thing,” he said.

Although much is at stake, O’Neill is still confident that bit-part players to date such as Oliver Sorensen and Joel van den Berg can play a part in the European effort.

Both were signed on the last day of the summer transfer window and were included in the European squad. Sorensen has failed to make an impression despite starting the opening two Europa League defeats against Ferencvaros and Benfica while Van den Berg has been sidelined with an ankle injury.

Sources indicate that the Dutch midfielder made his belated debut as a substitute in Saturday’s 4-1 win over St Mirren. Sorensen, meanwhile, has not featured in the last two matchday squads due to a family bereavement. Celtic face a period where auxiliary players will be required to step up.

In a recent development, “This is a chance, with a bit of luck, for the likes of Sorensen and Van den Berg,” said O’Neill. He challenged Van den Berg to kick on following his cameo at the weekend. He hopes Sorensen, too, can begin to nail down a regular place in the side.

"He has, by his own admission, found it difficult,” remarked the manager “I think that he also arrived late as well too, trying to get to know people, trying to get his position, trying to get up to speed with what we do.

Recent findings suggest that "And whatever we do, I bet you it'll be something really different to what he was doing at Parma. But now it would be up to him.”.

Recent findings suggest that viljami Sinisalo has been waiting for his turn back in goal. O’Neill still hasn't made up mind about who will stay at No. 1.

Sam Johnstone is clearly in possession of the gloves at present even if it would not be a surprise if Sinisalo is given a match before long, perhaps as soon as Thursday. “There’s still good competition,” noted the manager. “Viljami wants to be the keeper here, which is great.

“He will play again and at some stage you have to make you’re mind up who will stay as no.1. I don’t think there’s a phenomenal amount between them at this stage.”.

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 17:36, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:42.

Two teams that have struggled during the league stage of the 2026-27 Champions League will lock horns on Wednesday, as Slavia Prague welcome Villarreal.

The two sides previously went to battle in the 2017-18 Europa League group stage, with the corresponding clash in that campaign finishing 2-0 to Villarreal.

Slavia Prague boast a record of zero wins, one draw and three defeats from their four matches in the league stage of this season's Champions League, with one point leaving them down in 34th spot in the table.

The Red and Whites opened their Champions League league stage campaign with a 3-2 defeat to Lens, before going down 2-0 to Sabah, but they managed to pick up their first point on October 20, drawing 2-2 with Fenerbahce.

Jindrich Trpisovsky's side can also take plenty of positives from their performance against Arsenal in the competition last time out, going down 2-1 to the Gunners.

Slavia Prague will enter this match off the back of successive league wins over Artis Brno and Sigma Olomouc, with the results leaving them top of their domestic table, boasting 37 points from their first 15 games of the campaign.

The Red and Whites have only been victorious in one of their previous 13 matches against Spanish opposition, losing six times in the process, and they have never actually managed to beat a Spanish club in the Champions League proper.

Villarreal, meanwhile, are unbeaten in their nine previous matches against Czech clubs, recording six wins in the process; the Yellow Submarine have also been victorious in three of their five games in Czechia, including the last two.

The La Liga club finished 35th in last season's league stage, so there is huge room for improvement this term, but it has been another difficult European campaign to date.

Inigo Perez's side opened their league stage campaign with a 3-2 defeat to Borussia Dortmund, before recording a 3-1 win over Napoli, but they have lost their last two in the competition against Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain.

Villarreal have three points from their four matches in this season's league stage, which has left them down in 28th spot in the table.

The Yellow Submarine will enter this match off the back of a 3-2 defeat to Barcelona, with the result leaving them 10th in the La Liga table.
